title: Surasa
hook: the gods decide to test Hanuman, and they send the mother of serpents with her mouth wide open
carry: every time he gets bigger, she gets bigger

segments.voice: Yesterday: Mainaka, the winged mountain the wind once saved, repaying the debt to the wind's son. Your line was a breath of wind long ago. Did you hear a kindness from your family's past? Today, the second meeting over the sea. Day six hundred eight.

A job interview where the question has no right answer. A coach who keeps raising the bar every time you clear it. Some tests aren't trying to stop you; they're trying to see what you do when force won't work. Over the open sea, with Mainaka behind him, Hanuman flies straight into one of those. And the people who set it up aren't his enemies. They're the gods, who want to know what this monkey is really made of.
screen: `A QUESTION WITH NO RIGHT ANSWER.` → `THE GODS SET THE TEST.`

segments.voice: Valmiki says the gods, the celestial musicians and the great sages gather and talk it over. They turn to Surasa, the mother of the nagas, the serpent beings, and ask her to take a terrifying form and block Hanuman's way, so they can see his strength and his cleverness. Surasa agrees. She rises from the sea huge and frightening, and says to Hanuman: the gods have given you to me as food. You have to enter my mouth. Notice what Hanuman does first. He doesn't attack. He talks. He tells her, briefly and honestly, who he is and why he's here: Rama, the forest, Sita taken, the search. He asks her to let him pass. And then he makes a remarkable offer. Let me find Sita and tell Rama, he says, and I promise I'll come back and enter your mouth. That's a messenger speaking. The errand comes first, and his own life can wait in line behind it. Surasa refuses. She says she has a boon that no one can get past her. And she opens her mouth. So Hanuman grows, swelling to ten yojanas, too big to swallow. Surasa opens wider, twenty. He grows to thirty. She opens to forty. On and on they go, each matching the other, until her mouth gapes a hundred yojanas wide, as wide as the sea he's crossing. Every time he gets bigger, she gets bigger. Force is not going to settle this. Hanuman, hovering there, has to think of something else.
screen: `THE GODS ASK SURASA TO TEST HIM.` · `HANUMAN TALKS FIRST.` · `I'LL COME BACK, I PROMISE.` · then, large: `HE GROWS; SHE GROWS.`

segments.voice: Let the shoulders drop. Bring to mind a situation where pushing harder keeps making it worse: an argument that escalates, a problem that grows each time you force it. Picture it the way Hanuman sees Surasa, growing every time he grows. Now, for this sit, stop pushing. Let the breath get smaller and slower rather than bigger. Just rest in not escalating. The bell holds the time.
Surasa. The mother of serpents, sent by the gods to test Hanuman, whose mouth grows wider every time he grows bigger, until force can't win.
Your line: every time he gets bigger, she gets bigger. Today, when something grows every time you push it, try one move that isn't pushing harder. Day six hundred eight.

howItsDone: Storytellers telling the Sundara Kanda often pause on Surasa's growing mouth before revealing how Hanuman gets through.

pairs: let me finish, then I'll come back

myth: Surasa is sent by Ravana to stop Hanuman
the gods and sages ask her to test his strength and wit.
Hanuman first tries talking and explains his errand
he even promises to return and enter her mouth afterward.
every time he grows, Surasa opens her mouth wider.

fork.setup: you're Hanuman. a huge being blocks your path and says you must enter her mouth. what do you do first?
options: explain your errand and promise to come back afterward.
fork.reveal: Hanuman tells Surasa about Rama and Sita and offers to return and enter her mouth once his errand is done. she refuses.

original.note: Sanskrit surasā, the name of the mother of the nāgas in this story.

trapdoor: what you thought: Surasa is just another monster.
what it means: she's a test set by the gods to see Hanuman's strength and cleverness.
what a scholar hears: Valmiki frames the episode as a trial of Hanuman's qualities, and later tellings often read the three sea meetings (Mainaka, Surasa, Simhika) as a set.

sources.ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Sundara Kanda 1 (the gods ask Surasa to test Hanuman; the contest of growing)

notes: Sequence of sizes (10, 20, 30, 40 ... Surasa's mouth reaching 100 yojanas): confirm the figures in Sundara 1; the script states the exact numbers only for the opening steps and the end.
Hanuman's promise to return and enter her mouth after his errand: confirm.
Surasa's claim of a boon from the gods: confirm wording.
